messages.subject: Re: [seewave] Cut wave
messages.body_plain:
Le 31/05/2011 23:43, Paulo E. Cardoso a écrit :
> When analysing animal sound records, one will usually try to retain
> (e.g. with specprop() ) some parameters from calls.
> In order to analyse individual 'calls' , how can we 'auto-cut a wave
> file, isolating individual 'calls' to get parameters for each one? Is
> this feasible?
>
>

Dear Paulo,

Yes it is feasible with seewave 1.6.0 but this will be much easier and faster with the next version 1.6.1. You can get 1.6.1 here <http://rug.mnhn.fr/seewave/DEV/seewave_1.6.1.tar.gz> but I do not guarantee that this version is fully stable. It is still in devlopment and did not run the checks.

Anyway, here is the code for the first 'note' of the song 'tico'. You just need to write a loop to achieve the same for all 'notes' or 'calls' of the song you want to analyse

library(seewave)
data(tico)
pos <- timer(tico, f=22050, threshold=5, msmooth=c(50,0), plot=FALSE)
start <- pos$s.start
end <- pos$s.end
note1 <- cutw(tico, from=start[1], to=end[1], out="Wave")
spec <- meanspec(note1, plot=FALSE)
res <- specprop(spec)

Please be aware that the results of timer() might not be perfect. Check them graphically.

Feedback would be welcome.

HTH,

Jerome

messages.subject: absolute frequency values in meanspec
messages.body_plain:
How can one get frequency absolute values when running meanspec().
Default output seems to be dB values.
messages.body_snippet:
How can one get frequency absolute values when running meanspec().
Default output seems to be dB values.

messages.subject: Re: [seewave] absolute frequency values in meanspec
messages.body_plain:
Dear Paulo,

meanspec() returns by default relative values on a linear scale:

> data(tico)
> res <- meanspec(tico)
> head(res)
               x            y
[1,] 0.04306641 1.745206e-03
[2,] 0.08613281 8.832970e-04
[3,] 0.12919922 6.068424e-05
[4,] 0.17226563 6.161335e-05
[5,] 0.21533203 6.644111e-05
[6,] 0.25839844 6.503915e-05
> range(res[,2])     # range of relative amplitude values
[1] 5.699946e-05 1.000000e+00

Relative dB values are returned when setting the argument 'dB' (and
the argument 'dBref' if needed)

> resdB <- meanspec(tico, dB="max0")
> head(resdB)
               x         y
[1,] 0.04306641 -55.16307
[2,] 0.08613281 -61.07786
[3,] 0.12919922 -84.33848
[4,] 0.17226563 -84.20650
[5,] 0.21533203 -83.55126
[6,] 0.25839844 -83.73650
> range(resdB[,2])   # range of relative dB amplitude values
[1] -84.88259   0.00000

Best regards,

Jerome
